definition: Per-act HIV risk reduction while an agent holds an unexpired oral PrEP days-supply under the 30-day gap allowance. Value unchanged at 0.90 but the estimand is now explicit: it is NOT an intention-to-treat effectiveness, and cannot be one, since the claims-measured protected fraction of follow-up for oral is 0.46-0.54 by race and an ITT 0.90 over follow-up of that composition would imply on-treatment above unity. It descends from the legacy prep.adhr.dist/prep.adhr.or four-class framework with the zero-dose class deleted and renormalised, which is why it carries no coverage content and needs no correction now that discontinuation is measured directly. What it retains is within-fill non-ingestion, invisible to claims by construction: E = (1-f) x 0.954, where 0.954 is per-exposure protection conditional on at least 2 doses/week and f is the non-ingesting share of fill-covered person-time, so 0.90 implies f of 6-17%. Sensitivity range 0.80-0.95. NOTE: not race-stratified while the persistence half-lives are, so all racial variation in realised oral protection routes through persistence.

definition: CAB injection interval in time steps, and under the binary on/off primary the protective window as well. 9 (63 days), not the 8-week (56-day) label interval. Realized intervals are bimodal on a weekly grid with sharp spikes at exactly 56 days (n = 14,998) and exactly 63 days (n = 10,504), mean 59.1 and median 58: two scheduling conventions coexist, and clinics split between an 8-week and a 9-week reading of 'bimonthly'. At a 56-day window roughly 58% of maintenance intervals would generate at least one uncovered day for a patient on an ordinary clinic schedule, which is not a plausible description of protection lapsing. This is not a free upgrade for CAB and moves the protected-time target by about 12 points; the 56-day version stays as a first-class sensitivity. The asymmetry with oral (we credit no pharmacological tail past days supply) is defensible because a days-supply is what was dispensed while a label interval is a recommendation carrying a safety margin.

Gate the return hazard on an active risk indication. This is where risk enters the model once the seasons-of-risk DISCONTINUATION channel is retired: claims observe all-cause discontinuation and cannot decompose it, so the single measured hazard is fed in directly and risk moves to the return side. It is also the more behaviourally plausible placement, since people rarely stop the day risk lapses (they have pills in hand or an injection booked) but they do decline to restart.

Lapse ceiling on the re-initiation channel, in days. Beyond it an off-PrEP agent leaves the return pool and re-enters the naive initiation pool in prep_start(). Set at 730 because the measured return hazard in the 730+ window (0.0045/wk) is at or below the naive initiation rate (0.0057/0.0038/0.0058 by race), so classifying a multi-year lapser as experienced makes them slower to start than someone who never took PrEP; that window is also past the n>=100 support limit and is a flat extrapolation carrying about 55% of all off-PrEP person-time. It is also what gives prep.start.rate leverage in a coverage-expansion scenario: without it the naive pool empties over a long burn-in and a 50% rate increase moves coverage by 2.4 percentage points against the 10 the pre-rework model produced. Inf reproduces the previous behaviour.

When TRUE, a lenacapavir stopper uses the measured from-CAB destination composition with the two injectable destinations SWAPPED, so 'resume the modality I was on' carries the measured own-modality probability (0.89 falling to 0.43) and 'switch to the other injectable' carries the measured switch probability (0.009 to 0.051). This is an assumption rather than a measurement, and it is the conservative one: applying the from-CAB numbers unchanged would assert that a lenacapavir user who misses a dose switches to CAB 89% of the time, which is not a finding but an artefact of lenacapavir having barely existed in the 2022-25 extract. FALSE recovers the pooled behaviour.
